subject: MOVE statement
notes: kb/Work/PB428.md — the PARTIAL is DISCHARGED. SR3 designates literal-1 and the data item referenced by identifier-1 as MOVE's sending operands, so the row's surface is every literal-1 and every identifier-1 the language admits in that position, and the refutation held: of the eleven §8.4.3.1.2 identifier formats, Formats 5/6/8/9 are class object or pointer and excluded by SR1; Formats 1/2/3/10/11 were measured reachable through sendingOperand's literal / functionCall / dataReference arms; Format 4 — inline method invocation, §8.4.3.4 — was admitted NOWHERE, because the §8.7.4 invocation operator '::' had no lexer token at all and the rule bearing the construct's name matched `dataReference ( argumentList )` as a STATEMENT, a shape ISO defines nowhere. Now: COLONCOLON is a lexer token (§8.7.4; §8.3.5 rule 7 makes the two characters one lexical unit); `inlineMethodInvocation : objectReference inlineInvocationSegment+ refModPart*` implements the §8.4.3.4.2 general format rendered from the canonical PDF page 163 / printed folio 133, with the argument brace's five printed forms; and the alternative was added to the sending-operand rule (then MOVE's own, now the one sendingOperand, kb/Work PB2114) and to every other operand rule that admits a function-identifier — the Format-1 twin, whose exclusion §8.4.3.2.3 SR1 words identically to §8.4.3.4.3 SR1, so the two go in the same positions and no receiving rule takes either. MEASURED on this worktree's own cobol.exe: `MOVE OBJ :: "GETNAME" TO W` with a PIC X(8) RETURNING item yields "ACCOUNT " per §14.9.25.4 GR5, and the same designation carries the argument form, the chained form (§8.4.3.1.3 SR1), the class-name receiver, the ref-modified result (§8.4.3.1.4 GR1 g)) and an inline invocation as an argument of another. The DESIGNATION itself is still what MoveBinder.Bind builds and what every downstream sender-side rule reads off BoundMove.Source; the four-arm sending operand is now the complete surface SR3 designates. InlineMethodInvocationOperandDriftTests keeps the Format-1/Format-4 pairing mechanical over the .g4, so the next operand rule cannot reopen this gap silently. retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/CobolParserCore.g4#moveSendingOperand (kb/Work PB2114 unified the sending operand into the one sendingOperand rule; moveSendingOperand no longer exists)
